title: Genesis 28: The Charge and the Vow at Bethel
body:
Read the chapter → [Genesis 28](/bible/genesis/28)

## Introduction

This session read [Genesis 28](/bible/genesis/28) through 31 straight through and then opened the key points of each chapter. The recording of part one ends with the chapter 28 teaching; the teaching on chapters 29 through 31 in these notes comes from the part two recording of the session.

**[Genesis 28:1-4](/bible/genesis/28#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/genesis/28#v1)</sup> And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/genesis/28#v2)</sup> Arise, go to Padan–aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother’s father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother’s brother.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/genesis/28#v3)</sup> And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people;
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/genesis/28#v4)</sup> And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which God gave unto Abraham.

- Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and charged him: Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel, and take a wife of the daughters of Laban.
- The fathers from the beginning, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, married wives of their own kindred and were blessed in their children. Abraham gave the same charge for Isaac, and Isaac gives it to Jacob; the instruction was kept in the family line from the beginning.
- With the charge came the blessing of Abraham, passed now to Jacob and his seed: to be fruitful, to multiply into a multitude of people, and to inherit the land promised to Abraham.

  Precepts:
  - **[Tobit 4:12](/bible/tobit/4#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/tobit/4#v12)</sup> Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.

    The fathers from the beginning married wives of their own kindred; take a wife of the seed of thy fathers.
  - **[Genesis 24:2-4](/bible/genesis/24#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/genesis/24#v2)</sup> And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/genesis/24#v3)</sup> And I will make thee swear by the Lord, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/genesis/24#v4)</sup> But thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.

    Abraham made his servant swear the same charge for Isaac: no wife of the daughters of the Canaanites, but of his own kindred.

**[Genesis 28:5](/bible/genesis/28#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/genesis/28#v5)</sup> And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padan–aram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.

- Jacob was sent to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah. Rebekah herself was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother; the family line was kept in place, generation after generation going back to their own kindred.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 24:15](/bible/genesis/24#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/genesis/24#v15)</sup> And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

    Rebekah was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother; the marriages stayed within the kindred.

**[Genesis 28:6-9](/bible/genesis/28#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/genesis/28#v6)</sup> When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan–aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/genesis/28#v7)</sup> And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padan–aram;
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/genesis/28#v8)</sup> And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/genesis/28#v9)</sup> Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.

- Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father, but instead of following Jacob's path he went to Ishmael and took Mahalath to add to the wives he had. He answered his father's grief by doing his own thing.
- Esau had already taken Hittite wives that were a grief of mind unto Isaac and Rebekah, and his generations show wives of the daughters of Canaan. He was hardheaded from the beginning; that is the spirit of the wicked, who hate instruction and cast the words of the Most High behind them.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 26:34-35](/bible/genesis/26#v34)**
    > <sup>[34](/bible/genesis/26#v34)</sup> And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
    >
    > <sup>[35](/bible/genesis/26#v35)</sup> Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.

    Esau's Hittite wives were a grief of mind unto Isaac and Rebekah.
  - **[Genesis 36:2-3](/bible/genesis/36#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/genesis/36#v2)</sup> Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan; Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/genesis/36#v3)</sup> And Bashemath Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebajoth.

    Esau's generations confirm he took wives of the daughters of Canaan and of Ishmael.
  - **[Psalms 50:16-17](/bible/psalms/50#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/psalms/50#v16)</sup> But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/psalms/50#v17)</sup> Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.

    Unto the wicked God saith, Thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee; that is Esau's spirit.

**[Genesis 28:20-22](/bible/genesis/28#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/genesis/28#v20)</sup> And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/genesis/28#v21)</sup> So that I come again to my father’s house in peace; then shall the Lord be my God:
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/genesis/28#v22)</sup> And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God’s house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.

- Jacob vowed a vow: if God will be with me, and keep me in this way, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father's house in peace, then shall the Lord be my God; the stone set for a pillar shall be God's house, and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.
- A vow to the Most High is not to be made lightly. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better not to vow than to vow and not pay. Jacob vowed and rolled with the Most High, and he paid his vow.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiastes 5:4-6](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v4)</sup> When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v5)</sup> Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v6)</sup> Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

    When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
